verifierProblems.what: app/main/autostart.ts conflicts with fix/lifecycle (merge-tree: CONFLICT in autostart.ts). Lifecycle's emberWrote() decides whether a file without the X-Ember-Managed marker is an older Ember's entry: it compares every line of the file with entryLines(null, false), with Exec normalised. If TryExec is put into entryLines without a guard, either stringValue(command[0]) throws when command is null, or the legacy template gains a TryExec line that entries from 1b39bb3 don't have. Those entries then read as foreign, and the switch can never rewrite or remove them.
verifierProblems.fix: When resolving the conflict, add the line only when there is a command: `...(command ? [`TryExec=${stringValue(command[0])}`] : [])`, keeping the escaping helper. Add a case to autostart-owned.test.ts: an entry written by 1b39bb3's autostartEntry (no TryExec, no marker) is still emberWrote().

verifierProblems.what: README's Download section says each release has SHA256SUMS and tells users to run `sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS`. Nothing produces that file. There is no release workflow, ci.yml uploads the packages with no checksum file (I checked every fix branch's .github: none writes one), and docs/DEVELOPING.md has no publishing step. Whoever publishes 0.1.0 has no instruction to make it, so the check the README promises won't exist.
verifierProblems.fix: The docs package owns docs/**: add a short 'Publishing a release' paragraph to DEVELOPING.md. It lists the files to attach (the two RPMs, the AppImage, the Windows zip, and the mac-arm64 and mac-x64 dmg and zip) and the command `sha256sum ember-*.rpm Ember-*.AppImage Ember-*.zip Ember-*.dmg > SHA256SUMS`, which writes the 'hash  name' format sha256sum -c reads. Or have packaging add a CI step that writes SHA256SUMS next to the uploaded packages.

verifierProblems.what: The README's optional AppImage packages leave out pulseaudio-utils, which ember.spec Recommends. It provides parec, which Ember's speaker rejection needs (app/voice/speakers.ts); without it, decision V1 means a spoken request never counts as 'you asked for exactly that'. It also provides pactl, which the doctor uses to list microphones (its fix is 'sudo dnf install pulseaudio-utils'). An AppImage user who follows the README gets weaker voice behaviour.
verifierProblems.fix: Add pulseaudio-utils to the optional line, for example '# Optional, for "Hey Ember", speaking and Ember's desk: sudo dnf install pulseaudio-utils speech-dispatcher …'.

Decision V1, which fix/cmdcore's COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md text implements, counts spoken words only on Linux with speaker rejection and parec.
